_why: ONE table, two languages. `display_state()` lives in corral_core/sessions.py, and both web skins must mirror it in JavaScript -- the browser reduces events locally between polls, so it cannot ask the server what a pane means at the moment a permission card arrives. A mirror that is not pinned is a fork waiting to happen, so every case below is asserted against BOTH implementations: corral_core/test_display_state.py (python) and selftest_display.mjs in each skin (javascript). Full Corral's TUI reads the hub's `display` key and is pinned to this table's LEGACY column too, for the hub that predates it. Add a case here and every consumer has to answer it.
_fields: pane = the duck-typed attributes display_state reads (state, pending, gate_hold, idle_s, question, turn_via); want = the display state. `question` is the agent's open ask_human question (an object, or absent); `turn_via` is where the pane's most recent turn came from (null = the human's own send; `peer` = another pane's agent; otherwise a TURN_VIAS label). There is NO read-receipt input: the hub has no source for it, so each surface overlays its own (DESIGN-5 section 7).
_removal: deleted with display_state itself (DESIGN-5 S1, section 5).

cases.why: a fresh pane is working, not idle
mid-turn
a wedged adapter is still working, never idle -- the whole point of the uncertain state
just answered
one second inside the threshold
IDLE_DISPLAY_S exactly: the boundary belongs to idle
quiet for half an hour: this is what `idle` exists to say
a pending card is needs-you EVEN THOUGH the raw state says ready
the runbook gate parked it: no card, but only a human releases it
a gate hold on a stale pane still wants the human, not `idle`
the raw needs-you state with EMPTY pending and NO gate hold (the card not yet in `pending`)
a card outranks death: the core clears pending on exit, so where these overlap it is a bug and hiding it is worse
dead
restored from disk, deliberately not running: PAUSED -- a human must resume it, which is not the same as merely quiet
a freshly detached pane is paused too; age is not what makes it paused
an enum value this function does not know is NOT claimed to be working -- the raw label is rendered beside it
no state at all (a stripped object): treated as starting
ask_human: an open question is needs-you, not your-turn -- the whole defect was that it read like any finished pane
an open question does not age into idle: the agent is still waiting on the human
a question survives a hub restart (meta): the paused pane still wants the human
a turn another pane's agent started, now ended: the human did not start it, so it is not the human's turn
a rig's opening prompt ended: `rig up` sent it, not the human at the glass
a scripted consult turn is still the human's side of the wall: your-turn
the human's own turn (no via) ended: your-turn
a peer-started turn with a card pending still needs the human
a peer-started turn that asked the human is needs-you, not idle
a peer-started turn still running is working
